name: Belarusian folk sky
summary: Star lore still alive in Belarusian villages: Elijah’s Chariot, the Reapers, the Sieve and the Nail in the middle of the sky.

001.name: Elijah’s Chariot
001.description: The seven stars of the Plough (Big Dipper). The fiery chariot is driven by the prophet Elijah: this is the Christian version of an older figure that was simply seen as a “great cart”.

002.name: The Bride
002.description: The constellation Lyra, with the bright Vega in the middle.

003.name: The Chicks
003.description: The stars of the Pleiades, here chicks, just as in the Hungarian Brood Hen.

004.name: Peter’s Cross
004.description: The great cross of the constellation Cygnus: the cross of Saint Peter.

005.name: The Crown
005.description: The semicircle of Corona Borealis: the crown of thorns that was placed on Christ’s head.

006.name: The Goat
006.description: The bright Capella in the constellation Auriga. In Hungarian tradition it is also a goat: the Goat Kid.

007.name: The Grass Snakes
007.description: The V-shaped Hyades that form the head of Taurus, and Aldebaran: grass snakes.

008.name: Poland and Lithuania
008.description: The two bright stars of Gemini, Castor and Pollux, symbolising the two neighbouring states, the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Kingdom of Poland.

009.name: The Reapers
009.description: The three stars of Orion’s Belt stand one behind the other like reapers cutting a swath. In Hungarian tradition the same figure is the Reapers’ Star.

010.name: The Nail
010.description: The Pole Star: a nail around which the whole sky turns.

011.name: The Ploughman
011.description: The constellation Boötes with the bright Arcturus: a ploughing peasant.

012.name: The Rake
012.description: The fainter stars below Orion’s Belt: a rake.

013.name: The Ram
013.description: The four stars of the constellation Aries.

014.name: The Serpent
014.description: The constellation Draco. According to tradition, Saint George (Yuri) killed this serpent and hung it next to the star that always stays in one place, the Pole Star.

015.name: The Sieve
015.description: The faint star cluster of Coma Berenices. According to the saying, “God sifted the grain with this”.

016.name: The Little Cart
016.description: The stars of the Little Bear, the smaller copy of the great cart.

017.name: The Throne of the Lord Jesus
017.description: The bright stars of Orion: the throne of Jesus.

018.name: The Twins
018.description: The whole figure of the constellation Gemini.

019.name: The Wild Goat
019.description: The stars of the constellation Capricornus.

020.name: The Road of the Geese
020.description: Marked by one of the stars of Cassiopeia (Caph). The name refers to the route of migrating wild geese.
